reference_drawer.title: Substitution Method Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Rules and formulas to keep beside your notebook:

items.rule: A solution is an ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies both equations.
items.example: (2, 3) is a solution only when both equations become true.

items.rule: Rewrite one equation as x in terms of y or y in terms of x. Prefer a coefficient of 1 or -1.
Replace the isolated variable in the other equation. Use brackets around a multi-term expression.
Put the known value into the isolated equation to find the other variable.
items.example: If y = 3 and x = 7 - 2y, then x = 1.

items.rule: Check the ordered pair in both original equations.
items.example: Evaluate both original left sides separately.

items.rule: 0 = 0 gives infinitely many solutions; 0 = k, k not equal to 0 gives no solution.
items.example: A true identity means coincident lines.

concepts.title: 1. A pair means two conditions
concepts.subtitle: One ordered pair must satisfy both
concepts.summary: The solution is the ordered pair that makes both linear equations true at the same time.

points.text: Linear pair: Each variable has power 1, for example 2x + 3y = 12.
Solution: Checking only one equation is not enough.

concepts.formula: a_x + b_y + c_1 = 0,\quad a_2x + b_2y + c_2 = 0
concepts.trap: Do not call every point on one line a solution of the pair.

concepts.title: 2. Isolate one variable
concepts.subtitle: Choose the simpler equation first
concepts.summary: Rewrite one equation as x in terms of y or y in terms of x before substituting.

points.text: Easy choice: Prefer a variable with coefficient 1 or -1.
Sign care: A term changes sign when it crosses the equals sign.

concepts.title: 3. Substitute with brackets
concepts.subtitle: Reduce two variables to one
concepts.summary: Replace the chosen variable everywhere in the second equation and simplify carefully.

points.text: Replacement: If x = 8 - 2y, write 3(8 - 2y) when x is multiplied by 3.
Collect: After substitution, solve the resulting one-variable equation.

concepts.trap: Dropping brackets in 3(8 - 2y) changes the signs and gives a wrong answer.

concepts.title: 4. Back-substitute and verify
concepts.subtitle: Complete the ordered pair
concepts.summary: Find the second variable from the isolated equation, then test both values in both originals.

points.text: Back-substitution: Put the known value into the equation rearranged first.
Final check: Write two separate substitutions to catch errors.

concepts.trap: Report an ordered pair, not two unrelated numbers.

concepts.title: 5. Identity and contradiction
concepts.subtitle: Recognise special outcomes
concepts.summary: Substitution can show infinitely many solutions or no solution instead of one numerical pair.

points.text: Identity: 0 = 0 means both equations describe the same line.

concepts.trap: Do not force a numerical pair after an identity or contradiction.
